name: Crucible Industries Ember Rifle ER-7 'Ashfall'
description:
The ER-7 Ashfall fires thermite-tipped 6.5mm rounds that ignite on impact, combining ballistic trauma with incendiary effect. Crucible Industries developed the platform for anti-materiel operations where targets include equipment caches, vehicle fuel systems, and fortified positions with combustible components. Each round carries a 0.3-gram thermite payload in the projectile tip that activates on deformation.

The rifle itself is a conventional gas-operated platform built on the proven FR-9 receiver with modifications to the barrel lining and chamber to resist the thermal signature of the incendiary ammunition. A BCI-linked thermal scope provides targeting data overlaid with flammability analysis of the target environment — the system identifies combustible materials and predicts fire spread patterns to maximize incendiary effect.

The Ashfall is devastating against unarmored targets and soft vehicles but less effective against modern armor, which is designed to resist thermal penetration. Its real value is psychological — a single thermite round igniting inside a defensive position creates panic disproportionate to the actual damage. Fire is a primal fear that no amount of training fully eliminates.
specifications: caliber: 6.5mm thermite-tipped effective_range: 450m rate_of_fire: 600 rpm (cyclic) magazine_capacity: 25 rounds weight: 4.0 kg
tactical_use: The ER-7 excels in area denial and anti-materiel roles. Operators use the flammability analysis scope to identify high-value combustible targets — fuel storage, ammunition caches, communication equipment with flammable insulation — and deliver thermite rounds that create secondary fires. Against personnel, the psychological impact of incendiary ammunition frequently breaks defensive positions more effectively than superior volume of fire.
cultural_context: Incendiary weapons carry a stigma that other weapons do not. The Ashfall's operators are viewed with unease even by their own allies, and using thermite rounds against personnel in civilian areas is considered a war crime by most governance frameworks. Crucible markets the ER-7 exclusively as an anti-materiel platform, but everyone knows what thermite does to people.
story_hooks: An Ashfall operator accidentally ignited a chemical storage facility in a Tier 2 settlement, causing a fire that destroyed three city blocks. Crucible is trying to suppress the incident report.
Someone is using stolen ER-7 ammunition in a conventional rifle to commit arsons that look like industrial accidents — the thermite residue is being missed by standard forensics.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, aggressive assault rifle with a distinctly thermal aesthetic. The profile is angular and purposeful, with a noticeably reinforced barrel assembly that tapers slightly toward the muzzle. The design reads as purpose-built for a single, devastating function. Upper receiver slopes downward subtly, creating a predatory silhouette.
physical_description.dimensions: 960mm overall length, 78mm width at receiver, 145mm height with integrated scope. Barrel length 520mm.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced—4.0 kg distributes evenly across the platform. Front-heavy due to thermal-lined barrel assembly, but the gas piston system and receiver geometry keep it manageable for sustained fire.
physical_description.primary_material: Chromium-molybdenum steel receiver with thermal-resistant alloy barrel lining. Polymer furniture in heat-resistant composite. Picatinny rails are tool steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with heat-scorched aesthetic on barrel assembly. Upper receiver shows subtle oxidation patterns from thermal stress testing. Polymer furniture has a textured, almost charred appearance—intentional design mimicking exposure to its own weapon effects.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary, charcoal black accents, burnt orange/amber heat-stress discoloration along the barrel. Scope window is deep teal (BCI display color).
physical_description.grip_texture: Stippled polymer grip with minimal texture—designed to shed sweat and ash residue. Charging handle is knurled steel. Magazine well has subtle friction ridges.
distinctive_features: Reinforced, visibly thickened barrel assembly with cooling fins along the upper surface
Integrated BCI thermal scope mounted directly to receiver with teal-lit reticle visible through optics
Heat stress discoloration radiating from chamber—intentional burnishing showing the weapon's relationship with fire
Thermal indicator plate (red/orange color-shift material) beneath the charging handle—darkens when rifle reaches operational temperature
Magazine witness holes with thermite-round identification markings
Muzzle brake designed asymmetrically to redirect thermal bloom upward and away from shooter
Ambidextrous safety lever with textured detents
Proprietary magazine latch with slight lip design to stabilize heavier thermite-loaded rounds
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CRUCIBLE INDUSTRIES stamped in sharp serif font on the left side of the receiver, just behind the mag well. ER-7 'ASHFALL' engraved beneath in smaller caps. Serial number on the right side of lower receiver in six-digit format. Caliber marking (.6.5mm THERMITE) stamped on the barrel in white fill. BCI thermal scope has Crucible branding on the objective lens ring.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field weapons show carbon buildup around the chamber from thermite residue. Scorch marks and ash streaking on the barrel are normal. Well-maintained examples have clean optics and unstressed polymer, but the matte finish naturally conceals heavy use. Operators often see heat-browning on the bolt carrier from normal operation.
